Period: Apr 2019 to Sept 2023 (231 weekly changes). Both series are public and aggregate, so no personal data and no POPIA consent issue. | | Methods used | Smoothed cross-spectrum and squared coherence (modified Daniell kernel, hand-coded and validated against `spec.pgram`), phase-implied lead, pointwise F threshold, family-wise threshold from simulated independent series, simulation check of the method, bandwidth, differencing and subsample robustness, linear filtering. | ::: ## Question At which time scales, if any, do changes in Eskom's grid availability and JSE returns move together, and does either lead? ## Key findings
0.67

7.0 wk

0.026 vs 0.009
share above 1% line vs chance
- **Shared time scale.** The family-wise test does not reject the null of no shared frequency at the 5% level. The strongest association has squared coherence 0.67 at a period of about 7.0 weeks, against a family-wise threshold of 0.73. - **Breadth.** The share of frequencies above the pointwise 1% line is 0.026, against 0.009 expected by chance under independence. - **Direction.** Because coherence is not significant at the family-wise level, I do not interpret the phase. - **Robustness.** 1 of 6 alternative specifications (bandwidths, detrended EAF, two subsamples) reject at the 5% family-wise level. - **Method check.** The hand-coded coherence matches `spec.pgram` to within 1.6e-02, and a simulated 3-week lead is recovered as 2.91 weeks. **What this does and does not show.** Coherence measures linear association by time scale, not causation, and differencing removes the slow movements in which a multi-year recovery would sit. The Eskom data end in September 2023, so the findings cover 2019 to 2023 only. ![Left: squared coherence between the change in EAF and JSE returns, with pointwise (dashed) and family-wise (dotted) thresholds. Right: distribution of the peak coherence between independent series, with the observed peak marked.](figures/p2_headline.png){fig-alt="Two panels: squared coherence across periods with threshold lines, and the null distribution of peak coherence with the observed value."} ## What I would do differently I would use a longer window, since about 230 weekly observations resolve cycles slower than a year poorly and the Eskom file stops in September 2023. I would swap the All Share for an index of energy-intensive firms, and use wavelet coherence so the shared time scale can change through time, since load-shedding intensity changed sharply over the sample. ## Detailed analysis [Read the detailed analysis →](analysis.html){.pf-button} Code and data: [Code & Data appendix](../../appendix/code_and_data.qmd).
